title: When Knowledge Backfires: The Impact of Environmental Awareness and Attitudes on Pro-Environmental Behavior through the New Ecological Paradigm
text_snippet: When Knowledge Backfires: The Impact of Environmental Awareness and Attitudes on Pro-Environmental Behavior through the New Ecological Paradigm Abstract Ecological education is vital for fostering pro-environmental behavior by strengthening individuals’ knowledge, awareness, and attitudes. This study develops and tests an integrated model linking environmental knowledge, awareness, and attitudes to pro-environmental behavior (PEB) through the mediating role of the new ecological paradigm (NEP). Using survey data from 382 university students and structural equation modeling, the study finds that the proposed model demonstrates excellent fit. The results show a clear hierarchy of effects on the NEP. Environmental awareness is the strongest positive predictor ( β = 0.851, p β = 0.564, p = 0.017). The NEP, in turn, significantly predicts PEB ( β = 0.732, p = 0.019). Environmental knowledge has a significant negative association with the NEP ( β = −0.733, p = 0.039), suggesting that factual knowledge alone may not foster an ecological worldview without affective and value-based internalization. These findings challenge knowledge-deficit assumptions and indicate that the ecological worldview is shaped more strongly by awareness and affective orientation than by knowledge alone. title: Bringing Robotics into the Elementary School Classroom to Enhance Dynamic, Innovative, and Concrete Learning Environments in the 21st Century: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Bringing Robotics into the Elementary School Classroom to Enhance Dynamic, Innovative, and Concrete Learning Environments in the 21st Century: A Systematic Review Abstract The use of robots in elementary schools significantly enhances the development of dynamic and innovative learning environments in the 21st century. This study aims to analyze and explore various research publications that investigate how to bring robotics into elementary school classrooms to enhance dynamic, innovative, and concrete learning environments in the 21st century. The systematic review method rigorously examines, evaluates, analyzes, and interprets all study results related to the research subject. We obtained publications from three databases: Scopus, Web of Science, and Education Resources Information Center (ERIC), as well as Google Scholar, covering the period from 2013 to 2024. The results of the study indicate that robotics can serve as a powerful catalyst in elementary education, creating a more engaging, effective, and future-ready learning environment. The review concluded that while there are significant challenges in adding robotics to elementary education, the benefits-such as improved understanding, increased student interest, and the development of essential modern skills-far outweigh these difficulties, paving the way for new teaching and learning

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT Study Mode: Results from an Expert Rating Regarding Self-Regulated Learning
text_snippet: Evaluation of ChatGPT Study Mode: Results from an Expert Rating Regarding Self-Regulated Learning Abstract With the release of ChatGPT’s Study Mode in August 2025, the question arises as to what extent it aligns with established theories of learning, particularly self-regulated learning (SRL), and whether such applications can overcome previously identified barriers to learning with Gen AI, such as cognitive offloading. To answer these questions, the study examined the quality of Study Mode from an SRL perspective, its impact on student learning, and implications for research and practice. The expert rating was administered to SRL researchers. A total of 16 experts participated in fall 2025. The experts identified personalization and adaptive explanatory support as strengths. Concerns were raised regarding the tool’s potential to encourage offloading of metacognitive processes. The anticipated impact on students’ learning included both positive outcomes, such as improved understanding, and potential risks, including overreliance. The experts provide recommendations for SRL researchers, AI researchers, educators and students. title: Developing Visual-Analytical Competence in Teacher Education Through Art-Based Research
text_snippet: Developing Visual-Analytical Competence in Teacher Education Through Art-Based Research Abstract This article presents an experimental substantiation of the effectiveness of art research methods in developing the visual-analytical competence of future fine arts teachers. The study was conducted at Zhanibekov University (Shymkent, Kazakhstan) among 60 s-year students majoring in “Teacher of Art and Fine Arts.” A quasi-experimental “before-after” design was used, with control and experimental groups (n = 30 each). Over the course of 15 weeks, the experimental group implemented an art research program that included analyzing works of art, keeping visual diaries, completing reflective written assignments, and participating in group discussions. Assessment was carried out using four components of visual-analytical competence (cognitive, operational, interpretive, and reflexive-evaluative) and an integrated indicator. Statistical analysis included the Shapiro-Wilk test, paired Student’s t -test, and Mann-Whitney U -test. title: The Influence of Grit and Social Support on University Students’ Psychological Well-Being: The Mediating Role of Problem-Focused Coping
text_snippet: The Influence of Grit and Social Support on University Students’ Psychological Well-Being: The Mediating Role of Problem-Focused Coping Abstract This study aims to empirically test a theoretical model explaining how grit and social support influence university students’ psychological well-being through problem-focused coping. The novelty of this study lies in integrating grit (as a personal resource) and social support (as a conditional resource) within the framework of the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory to explain the mechanisms that sustain psychological well-being in the context of higher education in Indonesia. A quantitative correlational design was employed, involving 1,019 students from private universities in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, selected using cluster random sampling. Four validated instruments were used: the Psychological Well-Being Scale, Problem-Focused Coping Scale, Grit-S Scale, and Social Support Scale. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings demonstrate positive relationships among all variables: psychological well-being, grit, social support, and problem-focused coping. title: Benefits of Student Debate in Upper Secondary Education: A Scoping Review
text_snippet: Benefits of Student Debate in Upper Secondary Education: A Scoping Review Abstract Interest in student debate or structured debate in upper secondary education is growing in Portugal and other countries. While there is broad agreement on the benefits of debate for adolescent students, a comprehensive, up-to-date literature review on this topic is missing. For this reason, this study aims to analyse the extent, nature and results of peer-reviewed, published research on the benefits of student debate in upper secondary education over the past 25 years (1999–2023). A scoping review was conducted using Arksey and O’Malley’s framework, the PRISMA guidelines, a previously designed protocol, and 11 research databases. Fifty-six studies were selected. The studies revealed an increasing trend in both their number and geographical breadth, and highlighted the diversity of student debate regarding settings, concepts, and formats. As for the benefits, these studies provided evidence of the power of student debate to promote adolescents’ competencies, particularly in communication, argumentation, and critical thinking. title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Academic Performance of University Students in Ecuador
text_snippet: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Academic Performance of University Students in Ecuador Abstract This study examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the academic performance of university students in Ecuador, considering psychosocial variables such as technological self-efficacy, AI-related anxiety, intrinsic motivation, and social perception. Using a quantitative approach, data were collected from 698 students from various universities in the country through validated instruments measuring attitudes toward AI (GAAIS), anxiety associated with its use (AIAS), and perceived academic performance (RAU). The findings indicate that although AI tools are widely used, their direct association with higher academic performance is not statistically significant. However, negative attitudes toward AI, along with specific anxiety dimensions – such as anxiety related to learning and fear of labor replacement – emerged as significant predictors of academic performance, some with positive and others with negative effects. These results suggest that the impact of AI in higher education is not solely determined by technological access but is conditioned by emotional, cognitive, and contextual factors that influence its effective adoption. title: Architectural Design and Educational Psychology: A CABE-Based Analysis of Secondary School Environments in Turkey
text_snippet: Architectural Design and Educational Psychology: A CABE-Based Analysis of Secondary School Environments in Turkey Abstract This study presents the first systematic application of Commission for Architecture and the Built Environment (CABE) standards to Turkish secondary school environments, analyzing 12 public schools in Gaziantep through expert site evaluations and administrator surveys. Schools were assessed on organization, resources, safety, and successful whole dimensions using a 3-point scale, with Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) employed to identify distinct design patterns. Results revealed significant variation across CABE dimensions. Organization performed highest, particularly in movement paths, while resources, especially ventilation, required improvement. Most schools demonstrated adequate safety standards. The successful whole dimension showed greatest variation, indicating different alignments between design and user objectives. LPA identified four distinct school profiles: Resource-Constrained Balanced Schools, Well-Structured Safe Schools, Safety-Prioritized Challenged School, and High-Achieving Resource-Efficient Schools. title: Parental Support as a Mediator Between Teacher Support and Social-Emotional Competence Among Indonesian Gifted Students
text_snippet: Parental Support as a Mediator Between Teacher Support and Social-Emotional Competence Among Indonesian Gifted Students Abstract Gifted students’ success in life is not determined solely by cognitive intelligence, but also by social-emotional competence. These competencies are essential for building positive social relationships. This study examines the relationships among teacher support, parental support, and social-emotional competence among gifted students in Indonesia. A correlational research design involving three variables was employed. The participants were 190 junior and senior high school students aged 13–17 years. Students were selected based on institutional gifted-identification procedures, which included high academic achievement and standardized cognitive assessments. Social-emotional competence was measured using the Social Emotional Competence Questionnaire (SECQ), while teacher and parental support were measured using the Child and Adolescent Social Support Scale (CASSS). The data were analyzed using path analysis. The findings indicated significant positive associations among teacher support, parental support, and social-emotional competence. title: The Creativity-Centric Framework: Redefining Academic Performance through Task Completion and Cognitive Synergies
text_snippet: The Creativity-Centric Framework: Redefining Academic Performance through Task Completion and Cognitive Synergies Abstract In both the 21st-century academic and professional environments, the ability to plan, reflect, and adapt demonstrates the most vital function. Although creativity is acknowledged as one of the pillars, formal education systems still tend to deprioritize it, as their primary focus is on prior knowledge and critical thinking, rendering creativity’s role in task execution and performance irrelevant. This research fills that gap by proposing the Creativity-Centric Academic Performance Model (CCAPM), a new way of thinking that shifts the focus from what determines academic success to creativity. The CCAPM enables the development of a new creative concept that combines cognition and prior learning, viewing task accomplishment as a recursive cycle integrating real-world tasks and feedback. In contrast to other models, CCAPM approaches define creativity as the central aspect, rather than the tools built on thinking processes that aid and embellish task performance. The application of the model is meant to address the weaknesses in the educational processes. title: Open School Cultures and Educational Innovation: Evidence from a K–12 Principal Survey in Vietnam
text_snippet: Open School Cultures and Educational Innovation: Evidence from a K–12 Principal Survey in Vietnam Abstract Educational reform in Vietnam advances competency-based and student-centered practices, while policy directives prioritize creativity, collaboration, and technology-enabled teaching across school systems. Outcomes vary across schools, which highlights disparities in institutional conditions influencing the implementation of educational innovation processes. This study examines how open school culture is associated with educational innovation using survey data collected from 369 principals across primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary schools in different regions of Vietnam. Open school culture includes supportive and participatory leadership, teacher collaboration within professional learning communities, and Student engagement in classroom practices. Educational innovation is conceptualized as systematic change across pedagogy, curriculum, assessment, and digital practice within school contexts. Results indicate that open school culture explains 50 % of the variance in innovation outcomes, highlighting the central role of cultural conditions in shaping school-level change. title: We Must CHIL: A Comparative Study to Promote Global Citizenship across North–South Partnerships
text_snippet: We Must CHIL: A Comparative Study to Promote Global Citizenship across North–South Partnerships Abstract This study compares the effectiveness of Collaborative Hybrid International Learning (CHIL) and Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) in fostering global citizenship competencies through a reciprocal partnership between two private institutions, one in the United States and one in Ecuador. While COIL offers a cost-effective model for internationalizing the curriculum through virtual collaboration, CHIL extends the framework both conceptually and pedagogically by incorporating reciprocal, short-term in-person engagement rooted in equity-oriented and justice-driven internationalization. Using a mixed-methods quasi-experimental design, the research employed the Global Engagement Survey (GES), focus groups, and written reflections. Findings indicated that CHIL participants demonstrated greater gains in cultural humility, civic responsibility, and critical reflection compared to COIL participants. The study argues that CHIL represents a distinct theoretical evolution of COIL by positioning reciprocity, critical reflection, and North–South balance at the center of global learning.

title: Evaluating a Context-Aware Smart Home Prototype as Learning Media for Smart Green Building Education
text_snippet: Evaluating a Context-Aware Smart Home Prototype as Learning Media for Smart Green Building Education Abstract Smart home and green building technologies are increasingly relevant to energy efficiency, water conservation, security, and occupant comfort. However, integrated learning media that demonstrate these technologies in authentic educational settings remain limited, particularly in Indonesia. This study developed and evaluated a context-aware smart home prototype for use as learning media in smart green building education. Developed using the ADDIE framework, the prototype incorporated automation, Internet of Things (IoT)-based security, remote monitoring, automatic lighting and ventilation, greywater-supported irrigation, and a solar-tracking system. A qualitative feasibility assessment was conducted with 18 engineering students from Informatics Education, Building Engineering Education, and Mechanical Engineering Education through questionnaires and interviews. The findings indicate that students perceived the prototype positively in supporting their understanding of smart home functions and green building principles, particularly security, controllability, energy conservation, renewable-energy use, water efficiency, and comfort. title: Bhinneka Framework: A Holistic Approach to Enhance Critical Thinking in Engineering Education
text_snippet: Bhinneka Framework: A Holistic Approach to Enhance Critical Thinking in Engineering Education Abstract The 21st Century has witnessed innovations in educational methodologies because of global interconnectivity, digital advancements, and the increased availability of online learning resources. Such innovations have impacted on the engineering educational approaches towards problem-solving and knowledge creation. Contemporary educational practices place a premium on self-directed learning and the academic environment that fosters critical engagement with materials. An interdisciplinary approach that integrates pragmatic and entrepreneurial competencies with advanced technologies is also emphasized. The Bhinneka Framework proposes a solution. This research work illustrates how interdisciplinary approaches promoting student entrepreneurship, coupled with critical analysis, can bolster students’ order thinking skills. The variables considered in this research proposal include smartphone use, greater collegiate exposure, and an entire school philosophy. The research substantiated that the internet and entrepreneurship skills significantly promoted higher-order thinking skills. title: Integrating Assessment for Learning with Differentiated Instruction to Foster Students’ Mathematical Resilience
text_snippet: Integrating Assessment for Learning with Differentiated Instruction to Foster Students’ Mathematical Resilience Abstract Mathematical resilience is crucial for students’ academic success, yet many teaching methodologies overlook the anxiety and negative attitudes frequently associated with learning mathematics. This study examines the impact of integrating Assessment for Learning (AfL) and Differentiated Instruction (DI) on fostering mathematical resilience among elementary students. A quasi-experimental design was employed with 70 fifth graders divided into an experimental group ( n = 35) and a control group ( n = 35). The experimental group received mathematics instruction through a structured four-phase AfL-DI framework, while the control group was taught using conventional methods. Mathematical resilience was assessed through pre- and post-tests, and data were analyzed using Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA). Results indicated a statistically significant and statistically significant and large intervention effect on post-test scores after adjusting for pre-test scores, F (1, 67) = 236.63, p 2 = 0.779). title: The relationship between organizational functioning of low SES schools and teachers’ work-related wellbeing: the mediating effect of psychological empowerment
text_snippet: The relationship between organizational functioning of low SES schools and teachers’ work-related wellbeing: the mediating effect of psychological empowerment Abstract This study aims to examine the relationships between organizational characteristics of a school in a low socio-economic status (SES) environment and the work-related wellbeing of teachers. It explores how these factors are associated – both directly and indirectly – with teachers’ job satisfaction and feelings of job security, with psychological empowerment explored as a possible mechanism through which organizational characteristics are related to teachers’ job satisfaction and job security. Using a quantitative research approach, data was gathered from 33 low SES context schools in Lithuania, resulting in a final sample of 292 teachers. The findings indicate that in schools with low socio-economic status, teachers’ psychological empowerment helps explain the relationship between school organizational functioning and work-related wellbeing. As the organizational aspects of the school improve, there is an increase in teachers’ psychological empowerment. This increase in psychological empowerment, in turn, is related with higher job satisfaction and lower job insecurity for teachers. title: Integration of Lonto Leok Local Wisdom in Strengthening School Organizational Climate: A Sustainable and Innovative Approach in an Indonesian Context
text_snippet: Integration of Lonto Leok Local Wisdom in Strengthening School Organizational Climate: A Sustainable and Innovative Approach in an Indonesian Context Abstract This study addresses persistent challenges in schools, including limited transparency, ineffective leadership, unsupportive work environments, weak supervision, low community participation, poor communication, and insufficient collaboration and innovation. It aims to examine how integrating the local wisdom of Lonto Leok can strengthen the school organizational climate and identify innovative strategies to sustain these values within the educational framework. Using a qualitative descriptive design, the research involved principals, teachers, and school committee members from junior secondary schools in Manggarai Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. The findings reveal that most school community members understand the core values of Lonto Leok and consider their integration essential for enhancing leadership, participatory decision-making, conflict management, human resource development, and communication. To ensure sustainability, the study highlights the need for curriculum integration, extracurricular programs, professional development, collaboration with local communities, and the use of technology. title: Pedagogical System for Hybrid Training of Future Special Educators
text_snippet: Pedagogical System for Hybrid Training of Future Special Educators Abstract This article aims to examine the pedagogical system for hybrid training of future special educators. It explores the specifics of hybrid learning, including the use of digital technologies. The research employs survey and semi-structured interview methods, followed by statistical analysis, to gather and process quantitative data on the perceptions of hybrid learning among students and instructors during empirical investigation. The study intersects special education and educational technologies, presenting the latest statistical data for 2023–2024, which indicates a growing trend of hybrid learning implementation, reaching 97 % by 2021 due to the shift of educational institutions to remote learning. Statistical analysis revealed no significant ( p > 0.05) differences, as the variation between mean scores of the intermediate test was F = 0.31, p = 0.58, and between mean scores of the final test was F = 0.85, p = 0.36. This led to the conclusion of no correlation between learning effectiveness and its format. title: Socialization of junior schoolchildren with autism spectrum disorders in a comprehensive school
text_snippet: Socialization of junior schoolchildren with autism spectrum disorders in a comprehensive school Abstract The aim of this study was to examine the impact of a socialization program based on ABA therapy on the adaptive behavior and motivational orientations of primary school children with autism spectrum disorders. The study involved 130 children from the 1st and 2nd grades, divided into experimental and control groups. The intervention program included individual plans for social skills training, emotional support, and the use of interactive applications. The research methods included a quantitative analysis using the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scale and the “Let’s Do It Together” technique for assessing motivational orientations. title: Multivariate Analysis of the Performance of Industrial Engineering Programs in Colombia Based on Saber Pro Test
text_snippet: Multivariate Analysis of the Performance of Industrial Engineering Programs in Colombia Based on Saber Pro Test Abstract This study compares the academic performance profiles of 84 Industrial Engineering academic programs in Colombia based on results from the 2024 national standardized higher education test (Saber Pro). The main objective is to progress from an average to a classification process for academic programs, incorporating heterogeneous practices across academic competencies. The methodological pipeline is constructed on unsupervised machine learning methods: UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) was used to reduce the dimensionality of the data by keeping the complex local and global structure and K-means classification was used to group the academic programs. The optimal final number of clusters was calculated to be k = 3, determined both by elbow analysis and the average silhouette index. The programs were successfully clustered into three groups: high-performing (Cluster 1), intermediate-performing (Cluster 3), and low-performing (Cluster 2). title: Digital Educational Stories by Learning Disabilities Teachers in the Southern Region of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia: Employment, Obstacles, and Proposed Solutions
text_snippet: Digital Educational Stories by Learning Disabilities Teachers in the Southern Region of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia: Employment, Obstacles, and Proposed Solutions Abstract This study examined the level of digital educational story use among teachers of students with learning disabilities in the southern region of Saudi Arabia, as well as associated predictors, barriers, and proposed solutions. A mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 112 teachers (response rate = 74.7 %) using a validated questionnaire, and qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 20 experienced teachers. Overall use was moderate ( M = 2.93, SD = 0.81). Four-way ANOVA revealed significant effects for gender ( F (1,106) = 7.95, p = 0.006, η 2 = 0.07), years of experience ( F (1,106) = 15.48, p η 2 = 0.13), and academic qualification ( F (1,106) = 23.99, p η 2 = 0.18), while no regional differences were found. Qualitative findings identified barriers related to limited digital design competence, time constraints, insufficient formative assessment strategies, and lack of institutional support. Integration of findings suggests that effective digital storytelling implementation depends on structured professional development and systemic capacity building rather than technological availability alone. title: Exploring the Interrelation Between Open Innovation and Openness of University
text_snippet: Exploring the Interrelation Between Open Innovation and Openness of University Abstract Universities are increasingly compelled to function within an open and collaborative framework impacted by globalization, advancements in technology, and societal expectations. While the concepts of openness and open innovation are extensively examined within the higher education literature, their interrelationship remains inadequately explored from a conceptual standpoint. This research seeks to elucidate the relationship between university openness and open innovation by examining how university openness is reflected across the strategic, organizational, and mindset dimensions of open innovation within higher education institutions. The study employs a comprehensive literature review in conjunction with qualitative content analysis to systematically investigate the conceptual connections present in the existing academic discourse. The findings indicate that university openness manifests across these dimensions, supporting and strengthening the development of open innovation practices in higher education institutions. title: Dual Careers in Athletics: Needs and Expectations of Elite Track and Field Athletes
text_snippet: Dual Careers in Athletics: Needs and Expectations of Elite Track and Field Athletes Abstract Promoting the balance between academic achievement and sporting success has become a growing priority within elite sport. Mentoring athletes and preparing them for post-athletic life are key elements of modern sport governance, supported by various institutional and educational programs. The purpose of this study was to examine the expectations and needs of Hungarian elite track and field athletes regarding their dual careers. The research employed an online questionnaire developed within the Erasmus+ Dual Career for Athletes Competence (DC4AC) project, comprising 20 items rated on a Likert scale. The sample included 90 athletes (32.5 % of the eligible population) who had achieved 1st–8th place in national championships. title: Enhancing Cognitive Load, Collaboration Tendency, and Enjoyment Through 3D Augmented Reality in Engineering Education
text_snippet: Enhancing Cognitive Load, Collaboration Tendency, and Enjoyment Through 3D Augmented Reality in Engineering Education Abstract This study aims to explore the effect of using 3D Augmented Reality (AR) on cognitive load, collaboration tendency, and enjoyment in engineering education. A quasi-experimental design was conducted involving 111 students, divided into three groups: a control group (conventional), an experimental group with hints (AR + scaffolding), and an experimental group without hints (AR only). Data were collected through pretest-posttest scores and post-intervention questionnaires measuring Cognitive Load (CL), Collaboration Tendency (CT), and Enjoyment (EJ). Data analysis included normality tests (Shapiro–Wilk and Kolmogorov–Smirnov), Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test, Kruskal–Wallis test, One-Way ANOVA, and Multiple Linear Regression. Results showed that all groups experienced learning improvement, with the highest gains in the AR with hints group. Effect size analysis using Cohen’s d indicated a large impact of AR with hints ( d = 1.10) and moderate impact of AR without hints ( d = 0.63) compared to the control group. title: Pedagogical Intervention with a Mathematically Gifted Student from the Underground Profile: Case Study
text_snippet: Pedagogical Intervention with a Mathematically Gifted Student from the Underground Profile: Case Study Abstract The topic of gifted students has become the focus of the professional publications by a number of pedagogical researchers. Many of them point to the fact that the giftedness of these students is not always apparent in the school environment, so these students are often not identified as gifted. The article focuses on the pitfalls related to the identification of mathematically gifted students in the educational process and points to the reasons for this phenomenon. It presents the theory corresponding to this topic and follow-up research that deals with a case study using qualitative research methods. The selected case study focuses on a student who appeared to be mathematically gifted before entering primary education, but his giftedness did not manifest itself in the school environment. The student was observed by the researcher for a long period of time and was involved in a ten-month intervention aimed at cultivating his mathematical thinking and expression and developing metacognition through appropriately selected mathematical tasks. title: Moral Agency in Saudi Education: Defining Suitable Outcomes Within Curriculum Reform
text_snippet: Moral Agency in Saudi Education: Defining Suitable Outcomes Within Curriculum Reform Abstract This research explores the moral agency of teachers within the framework of Saudi Arabia’s education reform. The inclination toward Global Education Reform Movement elements, such as decentralization and preparing students for global competitiveness, necessitates investment in human capital for future competition and challenges. Ethnographic methods were utilized in this study. The study sample was a group of nine teachers from Saudi elementary and middle schools who specialize in family and everyday life skills. They participated in in-depth interviews during one academic semester. The findings of this research highlight that teachers’ moral agency in this setting has three main focus areas: (1) the importance of leading students toward moral integrity; (2) the importance of commitment to teaching family and everyday life skills; and (3) the importance of knowledge in teaching family and everyday life skills. The evidence illustrates that teachers’ moral agency is significantly influenced by their interaction with students, thus granting them a say in defining educational priorities.

title: Replication is Child’s Play
text_snippet: Replication is Child’s Play Abstract Open science teaching is becoming more common in higher education but introducing it to younger students can be equally valuable. Teaching open science early can prepare students for scientific careers, and enhance their scientific literacy, helping them navigate a world full of information that requires validation and critical reflection. We developed and delivered four workshops at a Belgian primary school centered around visual illusions and perception, reproducibility, and a replication study. In this article, we share our materials and reflect on our experiences regarding teaching open science concepts to children to assist others interested in implementing similar workshops. Our key insights include that it is possible to have fruitful discussions with this age group about psychological concepts, reproducibility, replication, and open science. However, it remains important to address challenges in science thoughtfully to maintain the children’s trust in science.

title: Digital Literacy as a Tool for Developing Computational Thinking in Young Learners: A Literature Review
text_snippet: Digital Literacy as a Tool for Developing Computational Thinking in Young Learners: A Literature Review Abstract The integration of digital literacy into educational systems has become a crucial factor in developing computational thinking (CT) skills among students. The review examines a range of methodological frameworks, national policies, and digital tools contributing to CT development. Findings reveal a strong interdependence between digital literacy and computational thinking: students with higher digital competence exhibit up to 30 % better performance in problem-solving, logical reasoning, and algorithmic tasks. Nevertheless, significant challenges remain, including digital inequality, insufficient access to infrastructure, lack of teacher preparedness, and curriculum fragmentation. The paper explores successful international initiatives – such as the Bebras Challenge, CodeWeek, CS Unplugged, and ISTE standards – as scalable models of integration. It also outlines effective strategies such as gamification, project-based learning, and adaptive platforms. Policy recommendations include the adoption of national digital education strategies and professional development for educators. title: Augmented Reality as a Supporting Tool for Building Mathematical Knowledge: The Case of Parallel Projection, Perpendicular Projection, and Representation of a Figure in Space
text_snippet: Augmented Reality as a Supporting Tool for Building Mathematical Knowledge: The Case of Parallel Projection, Perpendicular Projection, and Representation of a Figure in Space Abstract In the 11th-grade Vietnamese Mathematics Curriculum, content on parallel and perpendicular projection, and the representation of figures in space poses significant challenges for students due to the abstract nature of spatial geometry and limitations in spatial imagination. This study utilizes action research methods and GeoGebra 3D Calculator software to design AR-enhanced learning experiences aimed at addressing these difficulties. The study was conducted with 32 11th-grade students. To evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention, a historical comparison was made with the academic results of a cohort from the previous year ( n =40) who studied the same unit using traditional methods. The results demonstrate that the use of Augmented Reality (AR) effectively establishes a connection between reality and abstract knowledge. Critically, the post-test scores of the AR-assisted group (M = 8.2, SD = 1.1) were significantly higher than those of the historical control group (M = 6.5, SD = 1.5), with a large effect size (t (70) = 5.43, p

title: Exploration of Research Trends and Problem-Solving Themes in Computational Thinking for Higher Education Programming: A Bibliometric Study
text_snippet: Exploration of Research Trends and Problem-Solving Themes in Computational Thinking for Higher Education Programming: A Bibliometric Study Abstract Computational thinking (CT) has increasingly been recognized as an essential competency for supporting higher-order thinking in programming education. However, the extent to which CT research explicitly engages with problem-solving remains unclear. This study investigates publication trends and thematic structures in computational thinking research within higher education programming and examines how problem-solving is represented and interconnected within the body of literature. Using a bibliometric approach, 207 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2015 and 2025 were analyzed through VosViewer and Biblioshiny to examine publication patterns, keyword relationships, and thematic evolution. The results show a marked growth in CT-related publications from 2020 to 2023, yet explicit integration of CT and problem-solving remains relatively limited. Block-based programming appears primarily in introductory CT contexts, with text-based programming gaining prominence, but this is not closely connected to problem-solving themes. title: Gifted Students’ Experiences of Mathematics Education in Czech Schools: A Qualitative Study
text_snippet: Gifted Students’ Experiences of Mathematics Education in Czech Schools: A Qualitative Study Abstract This study examined the experiences of mathematically gifted students in mathematics education in Czech multi-year grammar and lower secondary schools, drawing on Self-Determination Theory (Ryan and Deci 2017). This area has received limited attention in existing research. Despite the prevalence of research focusing on teachers’ perspectives of gifted students, the voices of these students themselves have been largely overlooked (Gomez-Arizaga et al. 2020). The present study addresses this gap by emphasising students’ experiences through a qualitative design based on structured interviews with ten mathematically gifted students. The findings of the study indicated both differences and similarities between multi-year grammar school and lower secondary school students. Multi-year grammar school students appreciated structured lessons and often sought cognitive challenges. This suggests a clear preference for opportunities such as group work, flexible problem solving, competitions, and engaging tasks. title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Protecting Data Integrity within IoT-Based Educational Systems: A Scoping Review
text_snippet: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Protecting Data Integrity within IoT-Based Educational Systems: A Scoping Review Abstract The study explores the viability of artificial intelligence (AI) in securing data integrity upon implementation in IoT-enabled learning spaces. Under the regulatory framework of a scoping review grounded on PRISMA-ScR, we assess systematically how IoT- and AI-based technologies can be used to provide support for safety and privacy for smart learning spaces. By doing this, it will stimulate innovation and support proper utilization. The scoping review that is conducted takes into account the existing applications, benefits, obstacles, and gaps in knowledge to be able to properly address why multifaceted measures must be adopted for cybersecurity, data privacy, education equity, and reasoning that is algorithmic. Know that a series of crucial intermissions have been mapped, namely the non-explainability capability in AI technologies, the insufficient utilization of blockchain as a means for sound privacy security, and the improvement that must be addressed in the capability of intrusion detection systems (IDS) to function efficaciously within education networks. title: Which Learning Approach is More Effective on Self-Regulation Skills? A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis Study
text_snippet: Which Learning Approach is More Effective on Self-Regulation Skills? A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis Study Abstract Contemporary educational paradigms increasingly emphasise self-regulation as a cornerstone of academic achievement and lifelong learning. This study conducted a meta-analytic synthesis of various learning interventions targeting students’ self-regulation skills, drawing on experimental and quasi-experimental studies published between 2005 and 2025. Following a systematic search of Web of Science, ERIC, and Scopus databases, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analysed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA) V4.0 software. Although the Fail-Safe N indicated a robust overall effect, the funnel plot suggested a concentration of positive findings, meaning publication bias cannot be entirely ruled out. Results revealed that planned instructional programmes significantly enhance self-regulation skills, yielding a large effect size (Hedges’ g = 0.97). Exploratory moderator analyses further suggested that effect magnitude varied according to intervention duration, instructional strategy, and research design, though several subgroup confidence intervals remained wide and warrant cautious interpretation. title: The Power of Peer Communities in a Roma Student Society
text_snippet: The Power of Peer Communities in a Roma Student Society Abstract The paper highlights the importance of peer communities in supporting successful upward social mobility for underprivileged Roma university students in Hungary. There are many underrepresented student groups in higher education. One of these groups is comprised of Roma students, who experience difficulties in education especially when they lack sufficient systemic support. First-generation university students also undergo hardships in tertiary education. This paper introduces a Hungarian Roma Student Society that functions as an inclusive peer community for students who belong to these two underrepresented groups at the University of Pécs in Hungary. In the study, interviews with alumni student society members about their life experiences in school were conducted ( n = 50). To illustrate the importance of peers, eight interviews with alumni students living in the community were also selected ( n = 8). In this paper, the researchers utilize in-depth content and narrative analysis of the selected interviews. title: Unlocking the Healing Power of Writing in the Classroom: A Systematic Literature Review on the Implications for Educational Practices
text_snippet: Unlocking the Healing Power of Writing in the Classroom: A Systematic Literature Review on the Implications for Educational Practices Abstract Writing has emerged not only as a means of creative expression but also as a promising tool for promoting emotional well-being in educational settings. As students face increasing academic and personal pressures, the integration of writing interventions into classroom practices offers potential benefits for their holistic development. This study explores the healing potential of writing interventions in educational settings and their implications for student well-being. Using PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature review was conducted on 12 peer-reviewed studies published between 2013 and 2023. Findings indicate that writing practices such as journaling, expressive, and reflective writing can reduce stress, anxiety, and trauma while supporting identity formation and emotional regulation. The impact of these interventions is influenced by factors such as age, socio-cultural background, and prior trauma. Grounded in trauma-informed pedagogy and socio-emotional learning frameworks, writing emerges as a practical, low-cost strategy to enhance holistic student development. title: Advocacy Services in Primary School Social Work: Practice and Policy Recommendations in Vietnam
text_snippet: Advocacy Services in Primary School Social Work: Practice and Policy Recommendations in Vietnam Abstract The study aimed to determine the current situation and factors affecting the quality of advocacy services in primary school social work in Vietnam. A mixed-methods approach was utilized, integrating 398 quantitative surveys with 45 in-depth interviews to triangulate findings from teachers, social workers, and administrators. The research model includes five independent factors (Trust, Responsiveness, Service Performance Capacity, Empathy, Implementation Conditions), one mediating variable (Faith), one dependent variable (Satisfaction) and one moderating variable (Perception). The SEM analysis results showed that the above factors explained 44.9 % of the variation in Trust and 31.9 % of Satisfaction. Of which, “Trust” and “Empathy” have the strongest impact on “Faith”, while “Faith” strongly affects “Satisfaction” ( β = 0.539, f 2 = 0.411). On the contrary, “Service Perception” has a weak impact and does not play a clear moderating role. title: Do Programmes of Study Matter? Examining Academic Resilience and Students’ Academic Engagement in Second Cycle Institutions
text_snippet: Do Programmes of Study Matter? Examining Academic Resilience and Students’ Academic Engagement in Second Cycle Institutions Abstract This study investigated the influence of academic resilience on students’ engagement in second-cycle institutions and examined whether this relationship varies across different study programmes. Employing a descriptive research design, 301 students were sampled from a population of 1,496 using Slovin’s formula. Stratified and simple random sampling were used to sample participants. Data was analysed using PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap samples and the Kruskal-Wallis H -test. The analysis revealed that all dimensions of academic resilience: perseverance, reflective and adaptive help-seeking (RAHS), and negative emotional response regulation (NERS), significantly predicted all three dimensions of academic engagement. Programme-specific findings indicated that General Science students demonstrated the highest levels of resilience and engagement, followed by students in Home Economics and Business, while Visual Arts students scored the lowest. title: Extending the UTAUT Model with External Variables in Inclusive Schools: An Analysis of Teacher Satisfaction and AI-STEM Use Using SEM and ANN Models
text_snippet: Extending the UTAUT Model with External Variables in Inclusive Schools: An Analysis of Teacher Satisfaction and AI-STEM Use Using SEM and ANN Models Abstract This study investigates teacher satisfaction and the adoption of AI in inclusive STEM education in Indonesia. Despite the growing emphasis on AI integration in schools, there is a lack of studies on the specific issues of inclusive education for instructors and students. Out of 50,000 people, a statistically viable sample of 1,004 inclusive school teachers and students responded. SEM and ANN are used to analyse linear and nonlinear correlations between digital culture, facilitating conditions, AI literacy, and performance expectancy. SEM research indicates that digital culture, conducive environments, AI literacy, and performance expectancy all contribute to improved teacher satisfaction, with digital culture being the most significant factor. The ANN analysis emphasizes digital culture and institutional support, ranking each predictor. These findings indicate that organizational readiness and AI literacy are more crucial than ease of use or social influence for the adoption of AI. title: Assessment of E-Learning in Vocal Performance Training for Bachelor Students in Music Education Based on Shulman’s Signature Pedagogy
text_snippet: Assessment of E-Learning in Vocal Performance Training for Bachelor Students in Music Education Based on Shulman’s Signature Pedagogy Abstract This article presents an assessment of e-learning for bachelor students in music education as a means of preparing them for vocal performance, integrating the principles of L. Shulman’s signature pedagogy. The relevance of the study stems from the need to identify pedagogical approaches that enhance the quality of vocal-performance training for future music teachers. The research focuses on the following questions: how bachelor students perceive e-learning in the context of preparation for vocal performance within the framework of Shulman’s signature pedagogy; how an online course for this specialization can be designed; and how its effectiveness can be evaluated. To address these aims, the study employed questionnaires, quantitative methods, comparative analysis of mean values, and ANOVA. The findings indicated an improvement in students’ academic performance and a substantial development of their vocal-performance competencies. title: Marriage Obstacles for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities from Their Perspectives
text_snippet: Marriage Obstacles for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities from Their Perspectives Abstract Marriage is contentious social issue for persons with intellectual impairments, that their families and the individuals with disabilities themselves are divided on it. Some people look at marriage from a positive perspective that it helps them integrate into society and live a normal and independent life. But others believe marriage in such cases has many problems and it is not easy to succeed. This study aims to identify the main challenges faced by individuals with intellectual disabilities regarding marriage from their own perspective. The researchers created a questionnaire with 30 questions, divided into four main aspects: the nature of the disability itself, and the psychological, social, and economic challenges. The questionnaire was distributed it to a sample of 294 people with intellectual disabilities to understand their opinions on the matter.
